reconcileDrift: The local-data acceptance matrix now exposes concrete production gaps: ScreenDataManager lacks all destructive/local portability/repeat operations; backup is only an in-memory aggregate with no versioned archive bytes/createdAt or document I/O; restore/erase lack reminder coordination and full rollback; invalid errors are raw; restart fixtures do not close/reopen persistent storage.
goal: Complete the production local-data capability end to end within the data boundary: implement every missing CRUD/repeat/destructive ScreenDataManager command, a deterministic versioned single-archive byte codec with createdAt and injected document I/O, atomic replacement/erase compensation across database/settings/photos, stable localized error keys, reminder-reconciliation ports, and real close/reopen host fixtures. All destructive commands are reached only through the separate confirmed component path.
acceptanceCriteria: ProductionScreenDataManager supports typed delete zone/tray/recipe/batch/plan/observation, duplicate recipe, repeat batch, backup preview/restore/export/erase commands with strict validation and deduplication.
A deterministic versioned archive codec reads/writes one portable payload containing manifest createdAt, all managed records, preferences, photo bytes/checksums and no external path leakage.
Replacement restore validates entirely before mutation, replaces rather than merges, is duplicate-free, and compensates database/settings/photos at every injected failure boundary.
Erase atomically clears database, settings and app-owned photos and invokes an injected reminder-cancellation port; restore invokes an injected future-only reminder reconciliation port.
Validation failures expose stable locale-neutral error/resource keys suitable for EN/RU presentation, not raw technical exceptions.
Close/reopen file-backed SQLDelight and private-file fixtures prove restart restoration for every assigned restart/history scenario.
All assigned scenario tests and QG-012 fixtures pass without weakening existing assertions.
No Compose, root, platform-native, ledger or external project changes; specialist does not run Gradle. Any navigation-to-first-run hook remains an explicit root integration output.
